# ADDENDUM 24 — July 28, 2026 — THE STALE-SERVICE RECURRENCE, J4 BECOMES ARITHMETIC (VIDEO + THE J2 REVELATION), TRAJECTORY-LEVEL ANALYSIS, MOTION PROFILES, THE HIRING PLAN, AND THE LEARNING-STORE TRUTH
*(Appended in full. Nothing above this line was removed. One working day: the J4 saga's final acts — a recurrence traced to deployment staleness, the swing reframed as taught-endpoint arithmetic, the operator's video and his J2 observation splitting the motion into its true layers — plus the multi-engineer onboarding plan, the honest answers on what trains the proprietary model, and a batch of prompts that give the system trajectory eyes and cartesian transit options.)*

### Section 408: J4 recurrence — the fix that wasn't running

Operator ran the bowl program; J4 swung on the approach again, despite the July 27 verified fix (64.9°→0.8°). The recorder's `/api/runs` confirmed the run (`bowlpickplace_20260728T131129`, 53.9s) and the excursion class matched pre-fix — meaning **the fixed code and the running code were different things.** Diagnosis prompt issued: which staleness layer executed pre-fix code — (1) the service running pre-fix modules (never restarted after the fix session; verification had exercised offline regeneration rather than the service's own Run path) or (2) controller-resident stale Lua (does Run regenerate+push, or execute the resident project?). Fix per finding, plus **two guards shipped as the permanent answer**: (a) run-path hash self-check — every Run compares fresh-codegen hash vs what's about to execute, regenerates+pushes on mismatch, logs it; (b) **codegen version stamp** — generated Lua carries a header (codegen git-sha + timestamp) recorded in the run manifest, so `/api/runs` forever answers "which codegen produced this run's motion." Lesson codified: *verification must exercise the same path the operator's Run button does.*

### Section 409: The 7.6° reframe — endpoint arithmetic, and the option menu

Post-staleness, the measured residual was **7.6° on home→approach — endpoint delta, not excursion**: home's taught J4 ≈74° vs pick's ≈82°; the delta must happen somewhere, and the transit is where it lives. Claude Code presented a fix-strategy menu; decision recorded:
- **Option 1 DECLINED with reasoning:** seeding from the previous step's wrist would shift the rotation into the contact descent and demote it movL→movJ — the exact inversion of the operator's spec (vertical entry, orientation locked). Cosmetic transit motion must not be traded for joint-space rotation during precision entry.
- **Option 3 taken:** ship the attribution guards (§408's hash check + version stamp) regardless.
- **Option 2 (re-teach home's wrist) designated the real fix** — a training action, not a codegen one.

Subsequent operator direction — "use the link function instead of re-teaching" — surfaced the distinction: **linking means same pose entirely** (home would become the pick location); what's wanted is home's XYZ with pick's *wrist*. Resolution: one re-teach of home with J4/J5/J6 jogged to match pick's values — which linking then propagates to every referencing step in a single action (the feature doing exactly what it was built for). The J5 mention (later corrected to J4) hardened the plan to **align the whole wrist, all three joints, one visit** — the serial one-joint-per-session pattern named and ended. House rule proposed for the wizard copy: *teach every position in a program with a consistent wrist orientation unless the task demands otherwise.*

### Section 410: The video — and the J2 revelation

Operator supplied 28s of footage (whole arm, slow speed, well framed). Frame analysis confirmed: the tool assembly visibly reorients during the home→approach transit — the offset **camera boom sweeps a pronounced arc**, settling by the descent; the pick itself is clean. Two findings the tables couldn't give:
1. **The camera boom is a motion amplifier** — a ~100mm lever converting single-digit wrist degrees into an eye-catching sweep; the standing eyes-vs-tables disagreement partially explained as instrumentation (the tool now carries a pointer).
2. **Operator then spotted J2 rising and returning** — the shoulder, not the wrist. Reframe accepted: the objectionable motion is likely **two layers** — a small real wrist delta (the 7.6°, removable at the tablet) riding on the **movJ path shape** (joint interpolation humps the TCP mid-transit even between similar-height endpoints). The wrist re-teach cannot remove the hump; only changing the transit's motion type can. Every prior round had conflated the layers for lack of a per-joint, per-path view.

Honest positioning recorded when the operator pushed "re-teaching home has nothing to do with the swing": the move under complaint is *defined* by home as one of its endpoints; the swing is deterministic (same size, place, direction every run — the recorder proves it), and the re-teach is not a workaround but **the falsifiable experiment** — matched wrists either kill the swing (arithmetic) or exonerate the explanation in one run (defect, back to codegen). The 64.9° branch-flip monster and the 8° blend are different animals; one is already dead.

### Section 411: Trajectory-level analysis (prompt authored) — tracking between points

Operator: "you also need to track the movement in between points" — naming the excursion table's real blind spot: min/max/start/end per step discards the **path**. Prompt authored: per-step trajectory extraction from the recorder's existing 25Hz data — full joint timeseries + **FK-derived TCP path** (XYZ + RPY per sample), with the two numbers the table never computed: **TCP deviation from the straight line between endpoints (max + RMS, mm)** and **orientation deviation from endpoint-interpolated (deg)**; trajectory plots (joint-vs-time + the swept TCP path drawn as a polyline in the 3D twin — the view that matches what eyes see at the cell); the two new columns added to the excursion table so path deviation flags even when joint excursions look tame. Verification case: the latest bowl run's home→approach — the plot either shows the wander the operator films, or shows a clean arc and the conversation moves to expectations. *Video shows what eyes object to; the trajectory shows what the tool measurably did; together they end the interpretation gap.*

### Section 412: Motion profiles — Straight vs Fast (prompt authored)

Operator asked for a cartesian-hold option ("stay in cartesian mode during the motion path to maintain TCP orientation… or make the path more rigid"). Prompt authored: transit/derived steps gain `motion_profile: joint | straight` — program-level default + per-step override; "straight" emits the wire-verified movL to the same target; contact descents unchanged (always movL). **The safety mechanism that makes it a casual toggle:** codegen samples the straight-line pose path (~10 points) through seeded IK chained from the start joints — all samples in-branch with bounded inter-sample velocity → movL emitted; any failure (singularity proximity, branch break, unreachable) → **honest fallback to movJ with a validation note**, never a silent crash-course. Speed honesty noted (cartesian transits run slower; step copy says so). **"Smooth" (blending) explicitly excluded and gated** — no wire-verified blend syntax exists (July 22's crash; the capture session still owed); the UI must not offer smoothing yet. Closure geometry for the whole arc: straight transit kills the J2 hump and holds orientation regardless of wrist deltas; the wrist re-teach removes the endpoint delta anyway; before/after trajectory numbers + before/after video = the proof pair.

### Section 413: Speed ceiling to 100% (prompt authored, supersedes the 80% draft)

Operator first requested 80%, then 100% in the same session. Final prompt: `operator_speed_limit=100` at the config source; jog cap 50%, the >40% increase-confirm, server-side enforcement, and the asymmetry rule all explicitly unchanged and re-verified; UI reads the cap from driver-reported config. Standing cautions with teeth at 100%: **multi-pair programs stay off full speed until the two-pair anchor diagnostic runs** (wrong-anchor at 100% is a lunge); first 100% run = single-pair bowl, cell clear, eyes on the contact descents; per-step overrides (slow entry, fast transit) are the tool if descents look violent — never re-lowering the global cap.

### Section 414: Joint values in the teach drawer + the Match feature (prompt authored)

Operator (mid-re-teach-planning): joint values must render with the toggles in Joint mode. The §396 display prompt re-issued, tightened for the drawer: live angle above each joint's toggles (tabular-nums, 0.1°, never dropped), limits below (config-sourced, droppable in the drawer if the tablet height budget demands), proximity tint (amber 10°/red 3° from limit). **New addition — the "Match:" selector:** when teaching/re-teaching, an optional reference position renders that position's joint values as grey targets under each live angle, the live value greening within 0.5° — turning wrist-matching from photo-and-compare into **dial-to-green**. Built for exactly the pending re-teach; reusable every time the consistent-wrist rule needs applying.

### Section 415: PBD multiplicity — the three-bowl miss (prompt authored)

Operator demonstrated three bowls in a line, stacked at a destination; the draft produced ONE pick/place pair. Structural analysis: the correct program is a **repeated operation with per-iteration offsets** — pick advances by the row pitch, place climbs by the bowl height (one taught pick + one taught place + two offsets beats six teaches). Prompt: diagnose which stage dropped the count (intent vs composer); intent schema gains {count, pick_pattern: repeat_offset|individual|vision, place_pattern: fixed|stack|repeat_offset}; understanding-prompt vocabulary + few-shots for counts/arrangements ("three", "in a row", "stack", "on top of the previous"); **clarifications as the honest surface** ("3 bowls in a line — teach first + spacing (suggested) / teach each / vision each cycle"; stack height numeric with suggested value); composer emits taught pair #1 + derived iterations (reusing derived-step machinery + seeded IK); codegen unrolls (per-iteration offsets need controller variables we haven't captured — unroll and comment); the count-correction lands in the learning store as a premium structured signal. Pinned test: count=3 answer → persisted program contains 3 iterations.

### Section 416: Editable review + the corrections ledger (prompts authored)

Operator: no editing of the generated program before library save. Two-layer design, deliberately NOT a forked editor:
- **Inline parameter edits** in review (speed, offsets, dwell, IO, count/pitch/dz) via the SAME step-editor component the Program tab uses — edits live in the overlay model (like exclusions, keyed on step_key), surviving auto-recompose, with the rebuild-vs-keep guard on conflicts.
- **Structural editing** routes through **[Save & open in editor]** — persists via the full Accept binding, flags the program `draft:true` (DRAFT badge in the library until first editor save), lands in the real editor. Review edits parameters; the editor edits structure.

Operator's sharp follow-up — "how does the model know it did anything wrong if you can't edit in review?" — answered with the three-layer signal hierarchy: (1) clarification answers (cleanest, machine-readable); (2) review-time edits/exclusions as structured records {step_key, proposed, set} — **the highest-resolution capture point**, correction attached to the exact demo context; (3) the accepted-vs-final editor diff as the coarse safety net. Principle recorded: *every friction point between "I see the mistake" and "I can correct it" is a training signal lost* — editability in review isn't hiding mistakes from the model, it's how they're captured. **Addendum shipped into the prompt: the corrections ledger** — every review mutation writes a structured correction event at Accept; editor-first-save on a draft program appends the structural delta; `GET /api/pbd/{demo_id}/corrections` = the complete "what the model got wrong here" ledger; corrections-per-demo becomes the fine-tune-readiness metric.

### Section 417: The learning-store truth — what trains what, and where it lives

Operator asked directly: does the API-uploaded demonstration train our proprietary model, and where is the data? Honest answers recorded:
- **The API trains no one.** Interpretation calls to the frontier API are inference-only (provider does not retain/train — standing policy); the proprietary model **is not being trained yet** — the corpus accumulates.
- **Everything lives at `/opt/cobot/demonstrations/<demo_id>/`** — video, frames, transcript, structured intent, draft, clarification records, correction diffs, human_corrected.json. Model-proposed vs human-approved pairs are the future fine-tune's exact training rows.
- **The strategy restated:** frontier API as teacher while corrections accumulate; fine-tune a smaller open model on the corpus at the volume milestone (hundreds of corrected demos); Orin/cheap-cloud inference with API fallback for low confidence.
- **Two urgent actions:** the `/opt/cobot` backup (the company's most irreplaceable asset, zero redundancy, sliding since move prep — nightly tar+checksum to a second medium THIS WEEK) and the **dataset manifest** (demo/corrected/answer counts — the number for investor rooms and the fine-tune trigger; natural Engineer-A first artifact).

Related pipeline-locality question answered (§ "can building the program be internal?"): **composition already is** — the composer/codegen/seeded-IK stack is deterministic local Python (why recompose-at-Accept and 400ms auto-recompose are possible at all). Transcription goes local soon (Whisper-class on Orin — commodity, offline-capable, removes the internet-hiccup failure mode at customer sites). **Understanding stays external longest by design** — it's the teacher; cutting it off before the student has lessons inverts the strategy. Video understanding goes local **last**: when the corpus supports fine-tuning a Qwen-VL-class model for the narrow domain — a general small model today would reproduce the three-bowl miss, worse. Investor line recorded: *"the AI that builds the program is ours and runs on the robot; we rent frontier intelligence only for interpreting human demonstration — and every rental teaches the model that will replace it."*

### Section 419: Drag button, the stuck pose, and cell-scoped zones

- **Drag (free-drive) button non-functional** — documentation review: the flange button is *"user-definable, default free drag"* (HW §5.1.1); function assignable via **DI Function Configuration** (Start/Stop Dragging among the options — flange buttons at DI18–21); drag preconditions per the 16005–16012 error block: parameters initialized, **TCP/payload set** (the safety-test procedure's own instruction), Real Machine mode, pose permitting axis-lock. **Prime suspect: the controller's PayloadId preset never set for the 1.2kg vacuum tool** — drag's gravity compensation needs it (and the dashboard's own info banner says the controller uses its preset, not our program metadata). Checklist: set default load → verify the button's DI function mapping → init drag params if offered → test in Manual/enabled/mid-workspace with a hand under it. **Photograph the DI Function Configuration screen** while there (wire-truth never captured; Error Reset and Run Program as DI functions are cell-design material).
- **"Stuck in a pose, nowhere near collisions"** — read as the drag system's own refusal class (**16009: "Axis lock not possible at current pose — move to another pose first"**), a math refusal, not safety. Escape ladder: jog out via the pendant (drag isn't the only door) → if jog also refused, read the state banner/alarm/light honestly → toggle drag off/on if mid-drag frozen → full reset last. Carry-forward: if drag refusals surface nowhere in our UI, that silent-refusal gap is a small prompt.
- **Cell-scoped environment zones (prompt authored):** operator — "when a commissioned cell is not chosen, we should not have any bound limits." Design: zones belong to a cell profile (`cells/<cell_id>/env_zones` + active_cell pointer); **no cell → zero environment zones**; the robot-intrinsic guards (self-collision, ground plane, joint limits) are never cell-scoped and stay on; the current 6 zones (the OLD building's map, the live blocker) archive to `cells/old_shop_boyceville/`; active_cell defaults to none post-migration (immediate unblock); commissioning wizard owns zone creation; **an amber status chip ("No cell — environment guard off") makes the unmodeled state visible** — silence not an option.

### Section 420: The ROI math and the factory-UI shopping list

- **"How much time does it save?"** — the defensible arithmetic recorded: conventional pendant programming 1–4 hr/operation, a large program = 1–3 integrator days at $100–150/hr (or a two-week scheduling lead time for shops without in-house programmers); the NeuRobots path = demonstrate (minutes) + review (minutes) + teach contact poses only (2 per pair, not 6; linking dedupes shared poses) → **under an hour, by the machine operator**. Claim: **10–20× on programming labor; integrator dependence → zero for changes** — and the re-task case is the strongest math (weekly changeovers × minutes-not-days). Credibility caveats to volunteer: commissioning is comparable both ways; complex conditionals still mean editor work; corrections decrease over time per the flywheel. **Action: instrument the next big program build end-to-end and get an integrator quote for the same spec at Jade — one measured pair beats every rule-of-thumb in a pitch.**
- **Factory-UI shopping list consolidated (one ~40-minute session):** WIRE — (1) pause/resume verbs (Run→Pause→Resume→Pause→Stop; unblocks three gated features; answers freeze-vs-step-boundary); (2) blend/smoothing parameters (unlocks the excluded "Smooth" profile); (3) the delay/wait verb (a Wait-node save with-content HAR — the oldest open capture); (4) the healthy-stop shape (does their Stop send follow-ups our path lacks?); (5) bonus: single-step/breakpoint, mid-run speed change. CONFIG — (6) the payload preset (drag prerequisite); (7) photograph DI Function Configuration. Explicitly retired from the list: move/stop/IO verbs, the Lua dictionary, save/load, state streaming — all owned.

## PROCESS LESSONS (143–148)

143. **Verification must exercise the operator's Run button.** The J4 fix was real and verified — against offline regeneration, while the service process kept running pre-fix modules. A fix isn't shipped until the path the operator actually uses has produced the fixed behavior; the run-path hash check and the codegen version stamp make deployment staleness self-reporting forever.
144. **Deterministic is the opposite of random.** Same size, same place, same direction, every run = arithmetic, not defect. The 64.9° branch flip was a bug; the 7.6° blend is the difference between two taught endpoints. Distinguishing them is the difference between a codegen fix and a two-minute re-teach — and conflating them cost three sessions.
145. **A tool with a boom is a motion amplifier.** The offset camera arm converts single-digit wrist degrees into an eye-catching sweep — instrument-induced perception. When eyes and tables disagree, check what lever the eyes are watching before doubting either.
146. **Summary statistics hide paths.** Min/max/start/end per step adjudicated a question that was about trajectories; the J2 hump lived between the numbers. Track the movement between points: TCP line deviation and orientation deviation are what "moves straight" actually means.
147. **The re-teach is the experiment, not the workaround.** When the explanation is endpoint arithmetic, changing the endpoint is falsifiable science: the swing either dies (arithmetic confirmed) or survives (explanation dead, field narrowed) — one run, two minutes, no wasted outcome.
148. **Every friction point between seeing a mistake and correcting it is a training signal lost.** Editable review isn't a convenience feature — it's the highest-resolution correction-capture point in the flywheel, and the corrections ledger turns "how does the model learn it was wrong?" into a queryable answer per demo.

---

*Summary of Addendum 24: the day J4 stopped being a mystery and became arithmetic. A recurrence of the "fixed" swing was traced not to the fix but to its deployment — the service was running pre-fix code, verification had never exercised the operator's own Run path, and the permanent answer shipped as a run-path hash check plus a codegen version stamp in every run manifest. The residual 7.6° was reframed as taught-endpoint arithmetic (home's wrist vs pick's), the fix-strategy menu was answered by declining the clever option (it would have moved rotation into the precision descent) in favor of guards-now plus a wrist-alignment re-teach — reframed, when challenged, as the falsifiable experiment it is. The operator's video confirmed the sweep and added the revelation the tables had hidden: J2 rises and returns — the movJ path shape, a second layer under the wrist delta — answered by two authored prompts: trajectory-level analysis (TCP line and orientation deviation, the swept path drawn in the 3D twin) and per-step motion profiles (Straight = validated movL transits with honest movJ fallback; Smooth stays capture-gated). Around the motion arc, the day built the company: a two-engineer hiring plan with role seams, a day-one onboarding package, and interview material drawn from the project's own mysteries; the learning-store truth stated plainly (the API trains no one, the corpus at /opt/cobot trains the future model, the backup is urgent and still owed); the three-bowl multiplicity miss turned into an intent-schema upgrade with clarifications as the honest surface; editable review designed as overlay edits plus a corrections ledger that makes "what did the model get wrong here" a queryable endpoint; environment zones became cell-scoped so an uncommissioned cell stops hallucinating the old building's obstacles; the drag button got its documentation-derived checklist (payload preset first); the speed ceiling went to 100 with its cautions intact; and the factory UI's remaining debts were consolidated into one forty-minute shopping list. Six lessons, one amplifying camera boom, and the standing sentence that closes the arc: the swing is deterministic, the re-teach is the experiment, and the trajectory numbers will referee.*
